title: Platform-wide slowness and 429s
executive_summary: Starting ~19:55Z, request rate on api-gateway rose from ~1,195 to ~2,700 rps (peak 4,529), auth-service rose ~123% and user-service ~125%. CPU on gateway (to ~90%), auth (to ~77-86%) and user-service (to ~65%) rose in step. Gateway logs show the rate limiter flagging mobile-ios-7.4.0 retries at 314-396% of requests with Retry-After ignored, and that client is the top RPS source (~1,700 rps). The 429s are the rate limiter responding to this client. A similar past incident (HIST-2025-068) had the same mechanism. The user-service 7.1.3 deploy at 19:48Z is not supported as the cause: its metrics were flat until the surge, and it had no config changes. Confidence is moderate because no mobile release record was found and p99 latency did not clearly rise.

hypotheses.description: Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients ignoring Retry-After, driving traffic surge and resource saturation across api-gateway, auth-service and user-service. Mechanism: Retries from one client version multiply request volume about 2-3x starting 19:55Z. This saturates CPU on gateway, auth and user-service, and the gateway rate limiter returns 429s to clients. The surge precedes the 429s and the CPU rise, and the surge is attributed to a single client identity.

probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): traffic_surge in None - Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients ignoring Retry-After, driving traffic surge and resource saturation across api-gateway, auth-service and user-service.
corrective_actions: Enforce server-side rate limiting or blocking for mobile-ios-7.4.0 at the gateway, and cap retries for that client version
Coordinate with mobile to hotfix or force-upgrade clients that ignore Retry-After
Confirm the 7.1.3 user-service release is not implicated before closing
preventive_actions: Require clients to honour Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter, enforced in client SDK tests
Add per-client-version quotas and alerts on retry ratio
Add pre-release load testing for mobile API clients
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on request_rate per client_id and on retry ratio above 100%
Alert on gateway CPU above 70% sustained for 5 min
Monitor p99 latency on the user-facing endpoints, since gateway p99 did not show the reported slowness
limitations: Gateway and service p99 latency did not show the reported slowness, so the user-facing impact is not fully characterised
No mobile release telemetry was available
Redis and postgres were not queried
Client-level attribution rests on the gateway's per-client logs
[agent-reported gap] No mobile release or rollout record for mobile-ios-7.4.0
[agent-reported gap] No per-client traffic breakdown beyond log summaries
[agent-reported gap] No redis or postgres metrics
[agent-reported gap] No user-facing latency (e.g. RUM) data
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: INC-011's 429s and CPU saturation are best explained by a traffic surge from a single mobile client version (mobile-ios-7.4.0) that retries aggressively and ignores Retry-After. Traffic to api-gateway, auth-service and user-service roughly doubled-to-tripled starting 19:55Z, about 5 minutes before T0. The user-service deploy at 19:48Z (7.1.2 to 7.1.3, copy changes) is a weaker candidate: it preceded the surge, but no user-service latency or error change followed it. The 'slowness' symptom is not clearly visible in p99 latency at any of the three services, so the user-facing slowness is not fully explained.
